newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt eyes Baltic Shipping control.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt eyes Baltic Shipping control.

text.p: The Russian government wants to take a controlling stake in troubled Baltic Shipping but the scheme has not yet been worked out, a company official said on Wednesday.
"Tentatively, a controlling stake is under discussion, but what it will look like, nobody knows," an aide to chief executive Tatyana Chekalova told Reuters.
She said a September government resolution on state support for the merchant sea fleet provided for an increase of the government's 29.7 percent stake in AO Baltiiskoye Morskoye Parokhodstvo.
In 1995 the company's losses according to Russian accounting standards amounted to 215.82 billion roubles ($39.8 million), compared to 3.21 billion roubles in pretax profit in 1994.
The company's total debt to foreign creditors exceeds $300 million, Chekalova said. Its fleet has shrunk sharply in recent years and many of its ships have been arrested in foreign ports.
The company's biggest shareholder is the State Property Committee with 25.5 percent of shares. The St Petersburg regional property fund has 4.2 percent.

MI Maritime Investors (Holding) has 17.29 percent, MI Maritime Investors (Cyprus) has 9.05 percent, TOO Morflotinvest has 3.67 percent, AO Wall Street has 3.3 percent, AOZT Titan has 2.54 percent, AO Trustinvest has 2.21 percent.
--Konstantin Trifonov, St Petersburg newsroom (812) 219 9209 ($ = 5423 Russian Roubles)
